content.content:
# The record and the report

## What every report holds

Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.

A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.

A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.

If you have findings or decisions, put them in your report in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:

- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.

## The gap ledger

Each row is one claim. It has a status (`POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`), a class (`implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`) and how to reproduce it. The rows are under sections by area.

The rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

Reports everywhere cite rows by number. So never renumber or move a row. Give a new issue a new row with a new number. Close a fixed row in place.

The ledger is large: whole, it is about 400K tokens, and one row can be 12K characters. Never read it whole, and never print whole matching lines from it. To find rows, run the `ledger-find` query with a few words (below). If it reports many more rows, add a word. Then print each row that you need with `ledger:ROW`.

## FACTS and POSITIONS

FACTS and POSITIONS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry goes in `FACTS-history.md` and `POSITIONS-history.md`.

A FACTS entry is the fact, its source and its test in a few lines, under a bold title. It points to the report that holds the detail.

## The repository's history

- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`.
- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's.
- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a history walk from `HEAD` stops early. A `git log` of a directory is useless here. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. Do not read the big files whole. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:

    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh
    $T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'            # the FACTS.md entry whose bold title holds them
    $T 'section:HEADING'             # every FACTS.md entry of a section
    $T 'ledger-find:WORDS'           # each ledger row that holds every word: number, status, claim's start
    $T 'ledger:424'                  # one row of the gap ledger
    $T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'  # one of the curator's decisions
    $T 'index:WORDS'                 # the INDEX.md lines on a topic, one per note
    $T 'map:README.md#Touch this'    # a section of a note under explorations/coordinator/map/
    $T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'            # a section of any note, or of a .tex chapter
    $T --check ...                   # where each key matches and its size; --part N continues; --help

Cite a FACTS entry by its bold title, or by its opening words if it has no title.

## Writing to the record

- Add a fact to FACTS in the commit that establishes it. A decision of the curator enters POSITIONS in the next commit after the curator states it.
- Rewrite a wrong line of FACTS or POSITIONS in place.
- Write each thing in one place. The curator's words are written once, in POSITIONS. Everything else points there.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a standalone note there, write its INDEX line.

## Practices

- Cite a measurement that your brief cites or that your own work took, with its source. Take it again only if the code changed under it, and then say what changed.
- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.

## At a point to report

- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
- Then finish the work.
- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.
----
# Committing and pushing

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit your own files as you go, on the branch that you work on, and push that branch (below).

Scratch includes logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs and lists. Your tree's `tmp/` is gitignored. A private caches folder outside `tmp/` is not.

## What to commit

- Commit the Fortress change and its tests, your report if it is a file, and a reusable script.
- Commit your lines for the ledger, FACTS or the plan with your work (`records.md`, "Writing to the record").
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`.
- Do not commit a copyrighted PDF or deck. `research/decks/` is gitignored. Cite such a source by its Wayback URL. `research/extracts/` holds our own summaries, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.

## How to commit

- Commit as you go, each commit in one command. Never commit a directory copy, and never use `git add -A`:

      git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- Other agents may have uncommitted edits in the same tree. The command above commits none of them. Leave them alone.
- Before you commit a staged change of more than a few hundred lines, read `git diff --cached --stat`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer the harness suggests. If the work moves to another session, `explorations/protocol.md` gives the new session line.

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, do not push. That agent pushes right after it commits, so look again shortly. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push twice, in this order:

         git push origin main
         git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8

     The second push keeps current the branch that the container is re-provisioned from (the `cloud-container` skill, a lost container).
- Push no other branch unless your brief names it.

content.content:
# Process records: the common format

One record per run of the microGPT experiment, so that the runs can be compared on one basis later: how each explored this codebase, what it tried and dropped, what it delegated, what it cost, and what it found. A record is reconstructed from the run's transcript where one exists and from its committed files otherwise, by a worker that did not take part in the run. It records; it does not judge the result, which is the reviews' job.

Every record is one Markdown file in this directory, named `NN-<run>.md` in chronological order of the runs, one line per paragraph, with these sections in this order.

## Header

A table with exactly these rows.

| field | content |
|---|---|
| run | the run's name and the directory or files that hold its result |
| period | first and last timestamp of the run's work, from the transcript or the commits |
| strategy | one of: single long context; coordinator with delegated workers; external session without transcript; and a phrase saying how the work was split |
| models | the model of the main thread and of each kind of worker, as the transcript states them (never inferred) |
| delegations | how many, and to which model each; "none" if the run worked alone |
| tokens, main thread | output tokens and context tokens processed, summed over the run's assistant turns from the transcript's usage fields (output_tokens; input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens), stated to two significant figures; "not recorded" where there is no transcript |
| tokens, workers | the same sums over the workers' transcripts, or the totals their completion notices report |
| wall time | from first to last timestamp, and the active span if the transcript shows idle gaps |
| gates | which quality gates or process rules the run's brief imposed, and which it applied |
| outcome | program path, its verification result in one line, article path, number of gap rows, and the run's own process files if any |
| sources | the transcript file(s) and commits the record was reconstructed from |

## Timeline

Numbered phases in order. Each phase is a short paragraph: when it started, its goal, what was tried, what failed with the error or symptom in a few words, what was decided and why, and the evidence pointer (a probe file, a commit, a report). A phase is a change of goal, not a change of file. Dead ends are phases too.

## Dead ends

A table: attempt | why it was dropped | evidence. Everything that was built or tried and did not reach the result, including spellings, designs, tools and briefs that were rewritten.

## Delegations

A table: # | task as briefed, in one line | model | tokens | what came back and where it lives now. Include the delegated reports recovered verbatim beside the probes they cite (see below). "None" if the run did not delegate.

## Gaps found

Where the run's gap table is, how many rows it has, and which of its rows were already in the merged ledger at the time and which were new. No re-verification here.

## Findings

Five to ten sentences on the character of the strategy as the transcript shows it: how the run navigated the specification and the library, where it lost time, what it got right early, how it used or ignored the prior work in the tree, and how the result relates to the effort. Observations with evidence, no praise, no model comparison.

## Recovered reports

When a run delegated, each worker's final report is committed verbatim as a Markdown file beside the probes it cites (for example `explorations/run-b2/probes/REPORT-g1abc.md`), with a two-line provenance comment at the top naming the run, the date, the worker's model as the transcript states it, and the transcript file it was recovered from. The record's Delegations table links to those files.

# Round 1 — the first microGPT port

| field | content |
|---|---|
| run | Round 1, the first port: `explorations/microgpt.fss` (292 lines), with `explorations/micrograd.fss`, `explorations/mgbench.fss`, `explorations/names.txt`, the map `explorations/microgpt-port.md`, and the figures `explorations/fortify/microgpt-{value,model,attn}.tic` + light/dark SVGs |
| period | 2026-08-23T22:01:47Z (Pavol: "Add microgpt.fss port to the goals ideas list and start mapping what we have and what is missing") to 2026-08-24T00:05:58Z; commits `633a654d6` 22:05 through `1471048f0` 00:04 |
| strategy | single long context; one thread did target selection, feasibility mapping, the CPython baseline, the adversarial plan pass, all four implementation stages, the Fortify figures, the chart and the published page, with no worker and no worktree |
| models | main thread `claude-fable-5` (the `message.model` field on every assistant turn in the window); no workers |
| delegations | none |
| tokens, main thread | 246 assistant turns: output 3.1e5 tokens; context processed (input + cache creation + cache read) 1.2e8 tokens |
| tokens, workers | none |
| wall time | 2 h 04 min, essentially continuous; the one idle gap is 23:23:12–00:01:42 waiting on the 45-minute background training run |
| gates | Pavol's brief imposed one process gate — "Does your plan include good de-risking strategies for correctness and performance? Try adversarial review and improve. Then execute!" — plus the standing protocol rule that results are presented as a rendered artifact with a URL, and the stop hook's commit-and-push rule. The run applied the adversarial pass (it rewrote the map's risk section as "Risks and de-risking (v2)"), added a step-0 throughput microbenchmark as a go/no-go before writing the port, wired a golden check against a Python reference at 1e-9 into program start, cross-checked against a deterministic Python twin for bit-identity, and sized a nano config from the measured throughput |
| outcome | Program `explorations/microgpt.fss`; its `goldenCheck()` (15 logits over 3 positions, the mean loss and 5 parameter gradients against the Python reference, 1e-9) runs green at every program start, and the nano-config run (n_embd 8, 2 heads, block 8, 2,000 docs, 250 steps) went 3.29 → ~2.3 band in 45.4 min at 10.9 s/step against the CPython twin's 22 ms/step, with name-like samples (beller, aleia, alalein, alana). Article: the published page "A GPT You Can Read" (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ec92269d-059c-4f49-933f-fd9f9d5b953d) over `explorations/microgpt-port.md`. Gap rows: no gap table — the map's "Gaps" section lists five library gaps, and the syntax findings are recorded in prose in the staging entries. No process files |
| sources | `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6.jsonl` (records ~14193–14978); commits `633a654d6`, `4b9b1b926`, `352fdd6b0`, `5f7a31960`, `1471048f0` |

# Process record: microgpt-native (round 3)

Reconstructed in the common format of `explorations/process-records/FORMAT.md` by a worker that did not take part in the run. The coordinating session asked for this file at `explorations/process-records/02-microgpt-native.md` rather than the format's `NN-<run>.md` name.

Scope note: the run's design journal `explorations/microgpt-native.md` covers two programs — the index-formula rewrite `microgpt_native.fss` and the paper-register rewrite `microgpt_paper.fss` that Pavol's mid-run course correction produced — and then continues into the next run. This record covers the journal's entries from the handover brief to the adversarial review; entries dated 2026-08-27 and later belong to the microgpt2 run and are recorded in `explorations/process-records/04-microgpt2.md`.

## Header

| field | content |
|---|---|
| run | microgpt-native, the canonical-form rewrite of the verified transliteration; result in `explorations/microgpt_native.fss` (378 lines), `explorations/microgpt_paper.fss` (431 lines), the micrograd-scale alternatives `explorations/mgnative_{a,b,c}.fss`, the probes `explorations/nprobe.fss`, `explorations/tparallel.fss`, `explorations/compiler-probes/` and `explorations/spec-probes/`, the journal `explorations/microgpt-native.md`, the brief `explorations/microgpt-native-brief.md`, and the reports `microgpt-native-impl-report.md`, `microgpt-paper-impl-report.md`, `compiled-path-gaps.md`, `prng-findings.md`, `expressiveness-review.md`, `process-audit.md` |
| period | 2026-08-24T18:22:33Z (Pavol asks for a handover summary; the brief is written and committed as `5f1f92ca5` at 18:25) to 2026-08-26T06:57:30Z (the adversarial review committed as `fdb32514a` and reported). Pavol's verdict on the result came later, at 2026-08-27T04:06–04:14Z, and opened the next run |

The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in `Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it, not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).

The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). Between that library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation; it reports 1 error on the library since climb batch 9, unchanged by climb batch 10 (the `isLeftZero` pair of `LexicographicReduction`, row 582, his choice, one error at two locations; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/checker-count.txt`), 56 from climb batch 8, 59 from climb batch 7b (`FortressLibrary` 132 to 106 and `RangeInternals` 18 to 12 by rung L, the one library's refused overload families repaired by its own exclusions and `openRange`'s typecase: `MIN` 4, `MAX` 4, `openRangeHelper` 3, three juxtaposition and two `seq` errors gone, rung C's two `cond` errors cleared by L's api line), 75 from climb batch 7C (`FortressLibrary` 2 to 132 by rung Y, each error counted twice: `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause now checks as written, so the api's hierarchy pass no longer stops it and its 66 overloading and return-type errors are counted for the first time, row 459 closed; `RangeInternals` 18 unchanged), 10 from climb batch 7R (`RangeInternals` 42 to 18 by rung J, the one library's scalar ranges over `ZZ32` alone; `FortressLibrary` 2 unchanged), 22 from climb batch 7 (`FortressLibrary` 38 to 2, rung H having cleared the 18 instantiation-exclusion errors and the api still stopping at its hierarchy pass on `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, counted twice, item 21 of `coordinator/PLAN.md`; `NativeArray` 44 to 0 by rung A's `tabulate`; `RangeInternals` 42 unchanged), 62 from climb batch 6's rung F, which flattened the number tower (`FortressBuiltin` 18 to 0, `FortressLibrary` 110 to 38, `RangeInternals` 78 to 42, `NativeArray`'s 44 unchanged), through batch 6b, 125 from climb batch 4 through batch 5, 103 before it (rung N's declared rise: the 22 `fill` overloading errors in `NativeArray` that the crash it removed had hidden; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`, "The merged-diff review"), and the table of climb batch 10's landing, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/checker-count.txt`, is the next batch's comparand, as its distance table, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/distance.txt`, with its per-site list at `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, is the next distance stage's: 253 distinct errors over the whole library under the setting `any`, 87 fewer than batch 9's 340 (the typecheck kind 280 to 201), which was 225 fewer than batch 8's 565, itself 33 fewer than batch 7b's 598, which was 26 fewer than batch 6.5b's 624 (the overloading kind 148 to 123, rung L's families), which was three body errors in `FortressBuiltin`'s component fewer than batch N's 627, against batch 6.5's and 7C's 626, batch 7R's 627, batch 7's 940 and the baseline's 1,747 (`compile-ladder/gate-baseline/distance.txt`), reported and never red. Since `a2b4809a5` (2026-09-23) the count is reported and never red on its own, because a fix can raise it; the gate stays red on a crash line no rung declared, a stale shadow or a table with no total (`coordinator/FACTS.md` § The checker and the one library; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, the checker count). The route on the checker's multiple instantiation exclusion, the rule that no type may be two different instantiations of one generic, which 61 of batch 5's 125 errors came from, is decided, and climb batch 6's rung F carried it out on the one library (`coordinator/FACTS.md`, "The one library's number tower is flat"): route A, the rule kept and the library's numeric tower flattened, with the interpreter taught coercion first (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; the brief `reviews/exclusion-design-brief.md`; route C measured whole in `reviews/mie-probes/route-c-experiment.md`). How a `nat` size is carried at run time is decided too: design B, a size given th
e same descriptor object a type argument has, filling the slot the code generator already reserves (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`, revised after the three size probes and the cost measurement, `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md`, `size-cost.md`). The two probes that precede the run-time size rung's brief landed on 2026-09-25 (`perf-probes/nat/size-rung-probes.md`): a number's descriptor made by the loader on first request or by a factory with no holder class gives the same answers, the worker's reading, not a decision, being the factory, and the choice is one of Pavol's answers before batch 5 (`coordinator/PLAN.md`); and B's dispatcher already tests `DOT`'s shared size for equality, so no fix is needed.

Decided, in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`: the goal and its measuring stick (2026-09-16); test first, the test written and seen failing before the fix and kept in the corpus from then on (2026-09-17); the workflow, with workers pushing to their own `wip/` branches, the script in the repository and the higher tier called only at a refusal, a stop or a red gate (2026-09-18), narrowed to a judge's second ruling on the same rung or tree (2026-09-24); unboxed `double[]` storage and the `nat` sizes taken together, as the team designed them (2026-09-19); the tier rule, workers on the cheaper tier and a worker on the top tier only with his permission (2026-09-20); one library, the interpreter's, with no new declaration in the compiler prelude and its three files deleted at the switch-over (2026-09-21); route A and design B (2026-09-24, above), and the rows batch 3.5 handed back, 379, 380/381 and 383 (2026-09-24); re-approval rows 39 and 40 (2026-09-24, 2026-09-25) and 47 (2026-09-26). On 2026-09-26: a judge's second ruling runs on Fable; workers commit their own files as they go (protocol § 5); rung C's stop answered "(a), push", so batch 4 landed as gathered and was pushed; rung O's fork, the specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ declared in the interpreter's library first, then the ten natives raising `IntegerOverflow`, which also decides row 348 for the specification's spelling; S1, the team's layered form for a change to the specification; the later Types chapter (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`) cited beside `Specification/` where it speaks; S2, rung S taking the judgement's per-example verdicts; the number chapters changing only in the flattening rung's batch; and the plan, `coordinator/PLAN.md`.

What comes next is the plan Pavol approved on 2026-09-26, `coordinator/PLAN.md` (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26, the plan): its six phases from batch 5 to microGPT running fast, his answers in the order they are needed, the four workers sent out that day (W1-W4) and the parked items are there and are not repeated here. What is in flight at a given moment is in the boot note (`coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-19/held-list.md`, under "Boot note to the resumed coordinator", which is kept current at every compaction).

The last landing is climb batch 10, the run of `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-10.md`, item 8 of the plan's phase 3 (`coordinator/PLAN.md`, "Phase 3. The checker at a true zero"): item 20's drop with the one library's numbers', orderings', `List`'s and natives' slips (N), its generators', `Maybe`'s and reductions' slips (G), walk's Meet Rule for functional methods per providing type, the naked `Any` refused at load and a type parameter bounded only from above at its upper end (W), and the compiled checker's defects of batches 8 and 9, its varargs among them (C). It was cut from `9c9e823d5`, four rungs applied in the order N, G, W, C, the ascending order of each rung's lowest edited line in the files two rungs share (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/RECORD.md`, "The order the rungs were applied in"): N at `a1b5c253d`, G at `a9b9933e6`, W at `833420ce4` and C at `aa07efb31`, with the merged-diff review's corrections at `c14bbce87` and the landed hashes at `ec718967a`: the gate green on `aa07efb31` at its one run (`compileAll` in 48 s; `testFast` 1,826 tests in 48 suites, the compiler track 1,010 to 1,043, `LibraryJUTest` 86, every suite with no failure; `testSystem` 516 in four shards, 504 at batch 9, with no failure; 42 of 42 four-thread `atomic` runs; the ladder's 85 files and the eighteen microGPT components unmoved; the checker count 1, the same, declared none, the `isLeftZero` pair; the distance stage, reported and never red, 340 to 253, the typecheck kind 280 to 201, abstract-method 12 to 8 and export 8 to 4, `Stream`'s variance crash gone and the other three crash rows the same declarations at moved lines; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/summary.txt`, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/checker-count.txt` and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/distance.txt`, the next batch's comparands, with `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), pushed (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/RECORD.md`, "The gate"). The two microGPT check programs under walk were not run: the session's automatic permission check refused the commit stage's `coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh`, which runs `rm -rf` on its own work directories (`mg-run.sh:16`), and they have not been run on the landed tree; the way through is Pavol's, manual approval for the one run or an allow rule (the last entry under "Climb batch 10, listed for his review" in `coordinator/PLAN.md`). The specification was rebuilt once on the landed tree, 662 pages with no undefined reference (`ec718967a`). The stops met are lifted as reversible (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, "Reversible stops do not hold a batch."): rung N's three walk values changed by repairs of named sites, rung G's six walk stops now answering and one ill-typed program now refused, and rung W's parameter bounded only from above left at `BottomType` where its bound mentions another static parameter (row 612); rung C met none. The rungs', the gather's and the merged-diff review's items for Pavol are items 43 to 47, a sentence on item 38, a sentence on the parked line for rows 438, 441 and 445 ("Raised by climb batch 6's rung T") and entries under "Climb batch 10, listed for his review" in `coordinator/PLAN.md`. The combined post-batch review (`reviews/batch-10-review.md`, `c0d2e963b`) finds all four rungs in the spirit of his decisions and of the designers, rungs C and N made so by their refusals, with one stop met, rung W's, missing from his list (now an entry there), and its findings are routed in `coordinator/PLAN.md`, each at the home it names. Before it, climb batch 9 landed at `cec70988b` (rungs W, K, R and S; the count 56 to 1, the distance 565 to 340; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-9/RECORD.md`; its review `reviews/batch-9-review.md`) and climb batch 8 at `6416d216f` (rungs I, Q, O and M; the count 59 to 56, the distance 598 to 565; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-8/RECORD.md`; its review `reviews/batch-8-review.md`). The rung paragraphs of batches 8, 9 and 10 follow. Batch 7b's landing text and the paragraphs of batches 6.5b and 7b mo
ved to `microgpt-run-c-handover-history.md` when batch 10's review was routed, where the earlier landings are; each batch's own record is under `compile-ladder/` (`climb-batch-3/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-3.5/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-5/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-6/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-6b/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-7/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-7R/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-7C/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-6.5/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-N/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-6.5b/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-7b/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-8/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-9/RECORD.md`, `climb-batch-10/RECORD.md`; for the repair batch and batches 1 and 2, the gate summary and each rung's `record.md`).

**2026-10-02, climb batch 8 rung I (`rung-instance-bound`) landed as `f3032eed8`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-instance-bound` is not a parent: the compiled checker instantiates a type parameter nothing fixes at its bounds under the expected type, never `BottomType`, promotes a lone parameter's union to its bound, takes an intersection argument whole, and tries a call by subtyping without the expected type first; rows 447, 505, 508, 512, 515, 516 (compiled half), 518, 535 and 541 (checker) closed by their tests, row 425 noted (element type open); new rows 559 (an instance at an intersection dies at load, now reached by two routes, programs that ran on the base among them) and 560 (`fail` and `builtinPrimitive` refused where the bound gives no instance); inference chapter and its Appendix I entry revised in the S1 form; on its tree checker count 59 unchanged, distance 598 to 623.

**2026-10-02, climb batch 8 rung Q (`rung-numeral-library`) landed as `9d2e4c856`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-numeral-library` is not a parent: the one library's numeral type is the compiler library's `IntLiteral`, a sibling under `Number` with a coercion from it on each integer type, `QQ`, `RR64` and `AnyIntegral`, and its own declarations of the members of `Integral[\I\]` and the getters `zero` and `one` a numeral reached before through `ZZ32`; each integer type states its own comparisons, `CMP`, `MAXNUM`, `MINNUM` and numeral power, and `ZZ`'s api its arithmetic; row 517 and PLAN item 33 closed, row 454's integer half closed on the checker's side; walk's numeral stays an `Int` until Q-walk (`XXXNumeralWithNN32.fss` holds its `NN32` case). A numeral `IN` a `#` or `:` range and `(3).minimum` are refused by the checker over the one library since (rows 580 and 581). R9 (`NN32` into `RR64`) is not built: it conflicts with answer 8 (row 575), a fork for Pavol. On its tree count 59 to 58, distance 598 to 596.

**2026-10-02, climb batch 8 rung O (`rung-overloading-checker`) landed as `70d5486f9`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-overloading-checker` is not a parent: the compiled checker applies the Meet Rule for Functional Methods per providing type (row 556), reading in a component every declaration inherited from an api (row 568) and comparing the meet without the self parameter wherever it sits (row 569); it renames an inherited method's static parameters apart (row 561) and keys its overloading memo on its inputs (row 562); it reads an excludes clause's reciprocal entry with its parameters in scope (row 557), and types a character literal by each world's library (row 477); it checks no object expression per provider (row 570, home 2, masked by row 375), nor a component's own abstract functional method beside a concrete one inherited from another trait (row 572). Row 546's program is now accepted and fails at run time (row 566); two code-generation defects of functional methods with self not first are gated as expected failures (rows 571 and 573). On its tree distance 598 to 607 and count 59 to 83, the rise being the one library's per-provider pairs: 58 of the distance's sites in the apis and 44 in the components, 91 of them `CAP` and `IN` in `RangeInternals`.

**2026-10-02, climb batch 8 rung M (`rung-library-meets`) landed as `0ae526b31`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-library-meets` is not a parent: the Meet Rule pairs one type provides repaired by declarations on the meet, `String`'s juxtaposition moved to three top-level operators, 23 declarations retyped to what their bodies answer, rows 356, 472, 483 and 531 fixed and 473 partly; on its tree the count reads 39 (59) and the distance 545 (598); `isLeftZero`, the full sequential ranges' `map` and `distribute` left with rows 582, 583 and 433; the compiled overloading checker skips every symbolic operator (row 584), which hides `String`'s four sibling families (row 585); `UniformDistribution` over a strided range stops walk (row 586, home 2); `cross` is rung O's capture; batch 7b's two review-routed test files reworded and renamed.

**2026-10-03, climb batch 9 rung W (`rung-walk-instance`) landed as `669b77d03`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-walk-instance` is not a parent: walk instantiates a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes at its declared bound (row 424, plain half), a lone parameter with no narrowest candidate at its bound (row 516, walk half) and takes the bound for a join of several minimal supertypes (row 555); it throws `MatchFailure` from a typecase that matches nothing (row 558) and runs generic functional methods (row 567). The F-bounded half of row 424, a big operator's parameters (decision D2) and a parameter with several bounds walk cannot meet (row 591) stay at `BottomType`; a parameter that only another fixed parameter's bound mentions takes the arguments' type (row 592, decision D3); an untyped function expression's result and a parameter bounded only from above still fix `BottomType` (rows 587, 588). Each departure but D2 is gated by an expected failure. The inference chapter's two interpreter boxes and their Appendix I entry are revised and name each departure. New rows 587 to 594: 587 to 592 under walk or in the one library, 593 and 594 on the compiled path, gated by `XXX` pairs in `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`.

**2026-10-03, climb batch 9 rung K (`rung-walk-load-check`) landed as `7ed2a8387`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-walk-load-check` is not a parent: walk's harness names an expected refusal at load (`load_exception_contains` in `Name.test` beside a file of `ProjectFortress/tests/`); walk checks the main component's `comprises` clauses at load (row 551 for that component; another component's clauses and object expressions stay open, rows 551 and 597) and reads the overlap of a generic beside a plain declaration for every shape of static parameter (row 552); rows 22, 487, 534, 544, 549, 597 and 598 have expected failures by the key; reading the library's clauses waits on Pavol (rows 595, 596).

**2026-10-03, climb batch 9 rung R (`rung-range-meets`) landed as `631fb867e`**, one commit composed at the gather, of which `wip/rung-range-meets` is not a parent: the range types' 97 Meet Rule pairs have declarations on the meet and 55 range slips are repaired (rows 503, 580, 583, 586 closed); on its tree the count reads 1 (56) and the distance 416 (565); 36 sites left under rows 599 to 601, each for Pavol (items 39 to 41); `StridedFullRange3D`'s missing shifts gated as an expected failure (row 602), and the reversed sequential mapped range's new rendering pinned (row 603).

## 0. Scope, terms and method

Scope.

- Read-only. Main was at `a6b594799` when I started. The ledger last changed in `0cf66dbdb` (2026-10-03), so every number below is for that text.
- The ledger is `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`: 1,250,447 bytes, 1,219 lines.

Terms.

- **Row**: a table line that starts `| N |` above the heading `## Revival worklist`. There are 638.
- **Cell**: one of the eight columns `# | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround`.
- **Closed row**: a row whose defect was fixed. Section 2.7 shows five ways the ledger marks one.
- **Restatement** (this note's word for a duplicate): a later row that records the same defect at the same site as an earlier row, so that its claim could be one sentence of the earlier row.
- **Sibling**: a row with the same mechanism as another row at a different site, operation or path. It needs its own reproducer and fix.
- **Era**: a span of dates in which rows were entered the same way (the table in 1.1).
- **Length**: characters of the whole table line, counted by script. `awk` `length` counts bytes and gives totals 0.3% higher.
- **Climb batch**: one run of the batch workflow script (`explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`). It starts rung workers in parallel worktrees. **Rung**: one unit of a batch's work. **Skeptic**: an agent that checks a rung worker's work. **Judge**: an agent that rules between a worker and a skeptic. **Gather**: the stage that folds every rung's `record.md` (its finished lines for FACTS, the ledger and the handover) into the record files. **Merged-diff review**: the last review of a folded batch.
- **Run**: one of the microGPT ports of era A (`run-b`, `run-b2`, `run-c`, ...), each with its own `gaps.md`.
- **Home**: where a defect that a rung measures and does not repair is recorded (`climb-batch-workflow.js:1014-1018`). Home 1: repaired, with a passing assertion in the rung's test. Home 2: the specification settles it; an expected-failure test whose file name starts `XXX`. Home 3: the specification is silent; a test that pins today's behaviour and a ledger row.

Method.

- Rows. A script split each row on ` | ` and checked the result against `awk '/^## Revival worklist/{exit} /^\| [0-9]+ \|/'`. Row 83 sits in a seven-column table (section 1.5, item 2); every other row has eight cells.
- History. I read the file at each of the 175 commits that touch it (`git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` and `git show <commit>:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`). A row's era is the date of the first commit that holds its number.
- Instructions. I read `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` (search "ledger"), the batch `RECORD.md` files, the reviews and the skill.

# The territory map

## 0. Terms used here

Path: one of the two execution routes, the interpreter (`fortress <file>.fss`, "walk") or the compiler (`fortress compile` then `fortress run`); "both paths" means the shared front end.

World: which prelude a run links against; the interpreter world is `FortressLibrary` + `FortressBuiltin` + `AnyType`, the compiler world is `CompilerLibrary` + `CompilerBuiltin` + `CompilerAlgebra` + `AnyType` (`compiler/WellKnownNames.java:114-139`, `CompilerAlgebra` since `1bd8d3ad1`; `modules-and-phases.md` B.13).

Prelude: the library a world loads without an import; the compiler world's four components are 2,405 lines against the interpreter world's 5,314 (`wc -l` of the `.fss`; `spec-to-implementation.md` §2 names the files).

Switch-over: phase 4 of `coordinator/PLAN.md`, where the compiled path starts reading the interpreter's library and the compiler's own three prelude files are deleted, their tests kept (POSITIONS 2026-09-21, the library route); until then each path links its own world.

Gate: what a change must pass to land: on a clean build, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` at zero failures, thirteen compiled `atomic` programs three times at four threads, the ladder regression (85 files compiled and run against their baseline, the eighteen microGPT components compiled only) and the checker count, the compiled checker's errors over the interpreter's library, reported and never red on its own (protocol, hard rules; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`). Counts here are from climb batch 5's follow-up D gate (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/followup-D/gate/summary.txt`); the current ones are in the last landed `climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt`.

Shadow: a prototype of an edit to the original tree, made by compiling edited copies of the files and putting their class files ahead of the real ones on the classpath; no tracked file changes, and the gate cannot see it (`perf-probes/template-check/run-all.sh`; FACTS "The `nat` plan's minimal design works as a shadow").

Sealed tree: the original tree, everything outside `explorations/` and `research/`; sealed through `75cca6683` (POSITIONS 2026-09-17), editable since, each edit test first and flagged at commit (protocol, hard rules).

## 1. The five surveys, and the walkthrough beside them

`modules-and-phases.md`: the 22 packages with sizes, the import graph, the dead modules, the two pipelines phase by phase, the cache, the runtime, native interop, and the one-table divergence of the paths (B.14).

`spec-to-implementation.md`: the 53 chapters of the July 2012 draft, a table of about 110 features with the parser rule, checker class, interpreter, codegen and prelude location of each, and the layered picture of the numeric tower (§4).

`test-coverage.md`: the census of every test corpus and JUnit class, what the 1,377 and 382 are made of, the two corpora that never meet, the blind spots by module, and the loop timings.

`dormant-code.md` (part five, added at Pavol's request): the census of what is present, carries a design, and does not run: commented-out library declarations and `Library/incomplete/`, commented-out visitors and off-by-default flags in the source, commented-out test halves and the aspirational directories, the spec's genuinely dormant text and its 62 "not yet supported" notes, the papers; each item judged finished-unwired, sketch, superseded or unknown, and tied to a path step.

`design-intent-sources.md`: the five places rationale is written (in-repo papers, the Steele corpus, our extracts, the spec's draft-only notes and Internal Document, source comments and commits), and a table by design area of what intent the spec leaves unstated.

`compile-path-walkthrough.md` (part six, written 2026-09-20 for the checker decisions): the compile path followed end to end, one section per stage — parsing, name resolution and grammar expansion, the checker (what it walks, what it writes, its counts on the library before climb batch 4), the desugaring switches that make the paths differ, code generation, the second JVM and the stamping class loader, native bindings in both worlds, `nat`, and a glossary.

## 2. The shape of the system, in thirteen facts

The editable surface is about 149,000 hand-written Java lines and 19,900 Scala lines; the other 535,000 Java lines are generated and checked in (counted as in `modules-and-phases.md` A.1).

The AST in `nodes/` is the only intermediate representation from parse to bytecode; there is no lower IR and no optimizing middle (B.1).

# What the revival changed in Fortress, and whose Fortress the skill describes

## How to read this

- Short lists. Numbers as K or M. A term is defined where it first appears.
- **The team**: the Sun Labs designers. **The team's tree**: this repository at `a874948ac`, their last commit (2012-08-31). **The revival**: every commit after it.
- **Walk**: the interpreter, `bin/fortress P.fss`. **The compiled path**: `fortress compile` then `fortress run`; it makes JVM bytecode. **The checker**: the static type checker, written in Scala; it runs on the compiled path only.
- **The library**: the Fortress files in `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`. There are two. The interpreter's, `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`, is called **the one library** here, because the curator chose it to become the only one. The compiler's own, **the prelude** (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`), is deleted at the **switch-over**, the day the checker accepts the one library (POSITIONS, "The library route."; "The compiler prelude's leftovers go at the switch-over.").
- **Batch and rung**: a batch is one run of the climb workflow; a rung is one worker's piece of it. Batches are named 1 to 10 and 3.5, 6b, 7R, 7C, 6.5, 6.5b, N and 7b, after "the ladder climb" (eight rungs, 09-17) and "the repair batch" (09-18). Each batch's record is `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/RECORD.md`; batches 1 and 2 have `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` and `-2.md`. Which commits each batch landed is in `record-growth/landings.csv` (beside this note) and in section A10.
- **Row**: a line of the gap ledger, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`, cited by its number.
- **POSITIONS** holds the curator's decisions, **FACTS** what is established, both in `explorations/coordinator/`. A cited title is the entry's bold opening. **Answer N** is one of the curator's numbered answers of 2026-09-26 to 09-29 (answers 7 to 10 here).
- **Callout, S1 form, Appendix I**: how the revival changes the specification. A printed callout sits at the changed passage, and an entry in Appendix I (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`) quotes the original and gives the reason (POSITIONS, "The S1 form"). `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised specification: the Working Draft of 2011-02-02, byte for byte as the team left it.
- **Marks**. **[V]**: a programmer writing Fortress would notice it: a different answer, a program refused or accepted, or a different library declaration. **[I]**: internal.
- The tag `sealed-tree` is `75cca6683` (2026-09-16), the last commit before the revival edited the original sources. Its message: each later edit starts from a failing test added to the corpus (POSITIONS, "Test first, the test kept.").
- Evidence from the team's tree is cited as `a874948ac:path:line`, read with `git show a874948ac:path`.

## A. What the revival changed

### A0. The size of it

- 122 commits touched `ProjectFortress/`, `Library/`, `Specification/` or `build.xml` after `a874948ac`. 28 came before the tag (2026-08-18 to 08-23), 94 after it (2026-09-17 to 10-03). None has touched those paths since 10-03 (checked at `bb54e2113`).

- 43 of the team's own test and demo files have changed lines: 30 in `tests/`, 4 in `library_tests/`, 9 in `demos/`. New files: 146 in `tests/`, 491 in `compiler_tests/`, 32 in `library_tests/`. The suites: about 1.4K tests in `testFast` and 382 in `testSystem` on the team's tree, first run with the build moved to JDK 8 (`explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`); 1.8K and 516 at batch 10's gate (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/gate/summary.txt`).

## B. The skill's eleven points and the quiz: the team's Fortress, the revival's, or both

### B0. Method

- The eleven points are the bullets of "Fortress as a language" in `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/SKILL.md`, numbered 1 to 11 in the order the skill gives them: (1) only the compiled path checks types; (2) dispatch on every argument at run time; (3) functional methods; (4) traits and objects, no classes; (5) static parameters; (6) numbers are siblings, not a tower; (7) evaluation is parallel by default; (8) loops and reductions are library code; (9) juxtaposition is an operator and whitespace counts; (10) declarations; (11) specified, but not built.
- The quiz is `explorations/reviews/fortress-pretraining-quiz.md`: a fresh session's account of Fortress from pre-training alone, asked on 2026-10-08. The audit, `explorations/reviews/skills-distillation-audit.md` section B, grades each claim. It grades ten claims wrong or outdated, and trap 5 outdated for walk.
- Verdicts. **Team**: the team's Fortress, as the revival leaves it unchanged. **Revival**: what the revival decided or built. **Both**: say which part is which.
- The team's Fortress has two layers: the specification it wrote (`Specification-1.0-frozen/`) and the tree it left. A claim can be right about one and wrong about the other. The evidence names the layer.
- The revival's evidence is a commit from section A.
- Every "team" verdict below has an `a874948ac` file and line, or a frozen-specification file and line, read by me; none rests on the audit's grade alone.

### B1. The eleven points

1. **Only the compiled path checks types. Verdict: team, with a revival part in point 2.**
   - Team: the shell turns type checking on for `compile`, `link` and `build` and not for `walk` (`a874948ac:ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:403-407` against `:420-424`). FACTS, "The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path".
   - Revival: the shell is unchanged apart from a cache path. Walk gained load-time checks (W5, W6), which are not static types. The curator wants the checker usable on interpreter programs after the switch-over (POSITIONS, "The type checker on interpreter programs.").
2. **Dispatch on every argument at run time; the checker's three overloading rules; walk checks part at load. Verdict: both.**

# Plan: microGPT compiled on the JVM

The order Pavol approved on 2026-09-26 (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26, the plan). The evidence under it is the inventory `coordinator/open-items-2026-09-26.md`.

## Where we stand, 2026-09-26

- **Runs.** microGPT runs under walk. Both check programs pass 40 of 40 from an empty cache (inventory B3).
- **Stops.** On the compiled path, all 18 of microGPT's components stop at name resolution. The compiler's own library has no `Array`, `Char`, `ImmutableArray` or `Vector`. This has not moved since the baseline, and it is expected: the fix is the switch-over, not new names in the compiler's library (inventory B3).
- **Decided.** One library, the interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks (09-21). The exclusion rule is kept and the number tower flattened, with walk taught coercion first (route A, 09-24). Sizes get a descriptor at run time (design B, 09-24). The array design comes after the switch-over.
- **Landed.** Batches 1 to 4. Batch 4 taught walk coercion, taught the compiled checker `nat` and `int` sizes, and fixed the `ZZ32` shift count. The checker reports 125 errors on the interpreter's library (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`).
- **Decided, not built.** The specification rung S (S1 and S2 answered on 09-26); the wrapping operators ∔ ∸ ⨰, then rung O's overflow check; the run-time size rung; the flattening.

## The principle for the batches

Every batch lands with the specification, the library and both paths agreeing. So the work is grouped by what has to change together, not split finer.

Two rules of the batch machinery shape the order: two rungs in one batch may not change the same declaration, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, since every rung branches from the batch's base (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:465`, batch rule 1). That is why the wrapping operators and the flattening sit in different batches, and why rung O's check follows the operators.

How a phase-3 batch's content is chosen (the coordinator's method, as batch 10 was planned): the measure is the distance, the compiled checker's errors on the one library, and the source is the last landed gate's per-site list (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), every error with its site and class. The planner, an Opus worker, sorts it into three piles: (1) decided and free to fix, the library's one-off slips and the checker's defects with a known fix, which go into the batch; (2) waiting on a decision of Pavol's or a judgement (after batch 9: the arrays, 98, after the switch-over by his answer to batch 8's Q4; the self-typed bodies, 30, a list of ways and a judgement first; `isLeftZero` and items 37 to 42, his), which are held and listed in the record; (3) waiting on a probe, which is probed before the record is written (P1 for row 424's F-bounded half). Pile 1 gains the defects the last review routed as owed, the items this plan queues ("a checker rung after batch 8"), and his decisions ready to build (item 20). The pile is cut into rungs by code area, no two rungs on one declaration and none building on another (the two rules above), usually four, since one landing pays for them all and the harness runs two agents at once. Fable reviews the record in place; a question goes to Pavol only where a pile-2 item needs his word. There is no target size and no target cost per error: the planner takes what of pile 1 fits the rungs (batch 10: 148 of the 340, 192 held).

## The phases

### Phase 1. Batch 5: what is decided and shares nothing

- The wrapping operators ∔ ∸ ⨰ declared in the interpreter's library. The library bodies and the five team tests that rely on wrapping are rewritten with them. No output changes (inventory B1 step 13; POSITIONS 2026-09-26, rung O).
- Rung S: the specification revised for route A, except the number chapters. Everything it describes already runs on both paths (inventory B1 step 10; POSITIONS 2026-09-26, S1, S2 and the number chapters).
- The run-time size rung (design B): a sized program compiles, loads and dispatches on its size. Row 402's size case in the exclusion rule can land at its gather (inventory B1 step 12; POSITIONS 2026-09-24, design B).

Needs answers 1 to 5 below.

### Phase 2. Batch 6: the tower flips, the specification with it

<!-- How the gap ledger, FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX grew commit by commit from 2026-08-19 to 2026-10-08 (main at c9e6cfc85): the scripts, the data as CSV, one chart with each climb batch's landing marked, and what the chart shows; the earlier measure of 2026-10-02 extended to today and the ledger added. -->

# How the record grew, commit by commit

Four files are measured at every commit of `main`, from the first commit under `explorations/` (`446836590`, 2026-08-19) to `c9e6cfc85` (2026-10-08):

- the gap ledger, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`: characters and rows;
- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md` and `INDEX.md`: characters.

A row of the ledger is a table line that starts `| N |` above the heading `## Revival worklist`. Characters are Unicode code points. Bytes are in the CSV beside them.

## What the chart shows

`record-growth.png`, three panels on one time axis, a vertical line at each batch's landing:

- The ledger went from 83 rows (39.6K characters, 09-09) to 638 rows (1.25M) by batch 10 on 10-03, and has not changed since. Its first 309 rows (326K) came before the first climb; the 20 landings, with their run windows, added 16 rows and 46K characters each on average.
- From the ladder climb's start (09-17 06:01) to batch 10's landing (10-03 10:58), the batch run windows are 35% of the clock (135 of 389 hours) and hold 88% of the ledger's characters and 92% of its rows. They hold 22% of INDEX's growth and 26% of POSITIONS'.
- FACTS grew to 352K at batch 7b (09-30), then lost 92K in one commit on 10-02 (the rung entries cut to the fact), after a 55K rewrite on 09-20 and 44K on 09-30. It is 250K now. POSITIONS peaked at 105K (09-29), lost 34K in the rewrite of 09-30, and is 82K now.
- INDEX never lost more than 324 characters in a commit: 14K on 09-17, 143K now, a line for each note.
- After 10-03 the ledger stands still, and the three others gained 5K (FACTS), 11K (POSITIONS) and 9K (INDEX): commits about process, skills and the record, none about a batch.

## Files

Scripts, run from the repository root:

- `measure.py`: reads the four files at every first-parent commit with `git cat-file`, writes `series.csv`, `changes.csv`, `by-day.csv`, `top-additions.csv` and `per-batch.csv`. About 6 seconds. Needs `git` and Python 3.
- `classify.py`: who made a commit (coordinator, a worker, a batch's gather, a consolidation), by subject, paths and time, for `measure.py`.
- `chart.py`: draws `record-growth.png` from `series.csv` and `landings.csv`. Needs `matplotlib`.

Regenerate: `python3 explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-growth/measure.py`, then `python3 explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-growth/chart.py`.

Data (input, kept by hand):

- `landings.csv`: the 20 batches, the run's start (UTC), the landing commit and the code commits the landing records. The landing commit is the one that records the landed hashes and the gate summary (the repair batch: the commit that names the two hashes; batch 1: the gate summary; the ladder climb: its record and re-run). Landing time is read from git.
- `labels-2026-10-02.csv`: the class of each commit as the earlier worker labelled it on 2026-10-02 (regexes and hand corrections), kept as data.

Data (output of `measure.py`):

- `series.csv`: one row for each of the 1,618 first-parent commits: time, commit, the ledger's rows and characters, the characters and bytes of the four files, the batch whose landing it is.
- `changes.csv`: one row for each commit and file that changed the file (784 rows). Size, change in characters and bytes, class, batch, how many entries it added or lengthened and the three largest. A merge keeps its net change; the four side-branch commits it brought in have kind `branch_commit`.
- `by-day.csv`: characters added and removed for each file, UTC day and class.
- `top-additions.csv`: the ten largest single-commit additions of each file.
- `per-batch.csv`: the four sizes at each landing, and the change since the previous landing.

The earlier measure, carried over because the new chart does not hold it:

- `boot-size.csv`, `boot-size.png` and `boot-size-chart.py`: the size of the coordinator's boot (K tokens) at nine compactions, 09-19 to 09-30, from the session transcripts, with the sizes of FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX then. Not extended: the transcripts are not in the repository.

## Method and limits

- The line is `git log --first-parent` of `main`. A merge's net change is one step. The ledger's first commits were made on side branches, so on the line it first appears at 09-09 00:30 with 83 rows.
- Landing marks are the 20 commits of `landings.csv`. A batch's run window is its start to its landing.
- A class after 10-02 comes from `classify.py`'s regexes with no hand check, so it can be wrong. Sizes and rows are exact.
- The ledger's eras (A to E, rows by date, mean lengths) are in `../gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, sections 1.1 and 2.4. The row counts here agree with its eras: 309, 352, 454, 557 and 638 rows at the end of each.
- The chart's colours are slots 1 to 3 of the dataviz skill's reference palette (blue, orange, aqua), validated all-pairs in light mode; the ledger is neutral ink. The aqua line is direct-labelled, as its contrast needs.

Presentation only, not on the path, not an argument for Fortress; no work on it unless he asks.

11	
12	- **The project's end.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into phase three (2006) and the project lived on at Sun Labs until 2012. His reading: they did no work on performance, "mucked around with syntax", and the promise that a sufficiently advanced compiler would later make mathematical types fast was never true; the funding was pulled for good reason.
13	- **Boxed numerics.** The compiled path is only about ten times the interpreter because numerics are boxed (`FRR64`, no `DADD`); "without unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles, what are we even doing here". 23	- **The library's own practice is the standard.** "all the extensions that [microGPT] invented need to go directly to the standard library in the spirit of the standard library." - **Test first, the test kept.** Every sealed-tree edit starts from a failing test added to the corpus: the worker writes the test first, verifies that it actually fails, makes the fix, proves it passes, and the test stays in the corpus from then on; the full suite stays green. The unacceptable process is the one-off validation script, proving once by hand that the interpreter and the compiler agree and leaving no permanent check. The batches fix
- **The suite's verdict is the check.** A test passes or fails, as the team designed the suite, and a value that matters is asserted in the test with the mechanisms the suite already has (an `assert` in an interpreter test, `run_out_equals` in a compiled one): "what is the purpose of a test suit that you just cannot run it and get a green? If everything that's encoded in it is, is okay and it turns red if it's not, why would you have to compare s
- **Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.** "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt." The design, agreed with him and built into the batch script: the old code, the batch's base, is built once per batch, by the coordinator, before the launch, in a worktree nobody compiles or runs in (the script's `args.baseBuild`); "We just mechanically take the latest build and share it between each rung from the same b
- **The coordinator watches what it launches.** Only a long or large run the coordinator launches outside a batch, a probe that builds and runs suites for an hour or more, is watched against the estimate it was launched with, so that none runs away as probe P1 did (`coordinator/process-engineering/p1-cost.md`); when it passes its estimate the coordinator reacts, by an instruction to the worker or a stop, and its brief carries what keeps it effici
- **A deeper pass, not a halt.** When something goes wrong or turns out undecided, the answer is a deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. On a red gate over a merged batch, no bisection of commits: "we should identify the source of the conflict holistically and rework that part in the merged batch", because the goal is one tree with everything running rather than the largest subset that happens to be green. On a divergence the specification does 
- **Forks are probed before a batch is briefed.** "if there are known decision forks, which we can evaluate using probes, we should be doing these during this phase, during this planning phase": a fork a probe can settle is probed first, so that the decision is his and the worker gets a clean task, never a decision left to a worker and reviewed after the fact. Rows are taken one per message with refreshers (other languages, what makes sense in a 
- **A brief describes the problem, not the solution.** "How do we prevent the myopic view? … I want to have full creativity of solutions": a worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language and the library offer before a design choice reaches him; a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the library gets around it (protocol principle 2). A worker that records timings records the CPU too, so that comparisons can be guesse

The planner, who has the whole map, gives each rung a mission briefing from the map that its agents read in their first turn; the share of agents that use it is reported with each landing (it was about 80% once and fell to 25-35%: "We need to get back to that level"). The briefing is in neutral w
- **No re-measuring what the record holds.** "you are wasting resources on remeasuring." A rung whose test is the checker-count or distance stage takes the last landed gate's tables as its before and does not re-run the stage on an unchanged base; the ga
- **Reversible stops do not hold a batch.** A stop a batch record reserves for him (a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, an interpreter output a rung cannot account for): "These don't need me now. - **Which tier runs what.** "You can spend as much Opus workers as you want." - **The record is public and names models on purpose.** The protocol's rule against model identifiers is the harness's rule for what Claude itself writes and pushes, not a mandate to strip provenance from records that name models on purpose; "We are doing this work in public … there is no need to censor anything"; nothing in a transcript or an index is held back from the tree for that reason. # Post-mortem of 2026-09-29: the batch practice

Opened at Pavol's word (19:21:03 UTC on 2026-09-29): "The archaeology must be committed. We are now performing a new post-mortem. Mark it with today's date. We are reviewing our procedures like we did previously. All this goes on record so that the failures of the models can be remedied and that the anthropic researchers who think they know what software development is and how software development is solved and be shamed publicly."

## What set it off

Batch 6.5b landed at `e3214cbf1`. Measured from its base `382b9fe7f` to its landing, the change to Fortress itself was about 280 lines of library, interpreter and checker code, 90 lines of specification text and 710 lines of tests. Beside it the batch committed 866 record files, 46K lines: 14 reports (1.9K lines), 228 captured run outputs (37K lines, the largest a 17K-line LaTeX build log), 247 probe programs and test drafts, 377 scripts and small files; 583 of the 866 are named by no report or record. The run took 17 agents, 6.15M tokens by the reviews' measure, and 7 h 43 min (`explorations/reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`). Pavol's reading (18:25 UTC): "Those are scratch that got committed anyway. … We must adjust our practice. This is unsustainable." "I do not recall that I have voluntarily accepted to be committing all these log files together with the batches." And on the output comparison each rung runs three times over the whole interpreter corpus (18:52 UTC): "why would you have to run it multiple times at the beginning to establish some kind of baseline? … if it's necessary … then we need to redesign how the test suite for Fortress is working."

His points, held while he reads, are the four groups of 18:25 to 18:52 UTC in `../postmortem-2026-09-19/held-list.md`, under "Held while he reads".

## What is here

- `characterization.md`: every batch from git (what each changed in Fortress, what it committed beside that, cited against uncited, its coordinator-record churn and ledger rows), the token spend of every run by stage, and the revival's tests measured against the team's test-suite practice; ten read-only readers of workflow `wf_576bd1f3-f0c`, their sections as returned.
- `measures-6.5b.md`: the coordinator's measurements of batch 6.5b given to Pavol in chat (what it changed in Fortress, what it committed beside that, its tokens by stage, the 18 tests that vary from run to run, all the team's).
- `archaeology-testing.md`: where the testing practice and the skeptic came from, by a Sonnet archaeology worker: Pavol's words on test-first (a failing test written first, seen failing, then the fix, a permanent check, never a captured file), the skeptic as the coordinator's role with an adversarial default, the recorded failure's growth step by step, the reviews that never questioned it, where it drifted with first commits, and his hypothesis that his ask for an adversarial skeptic was the original sin (in part, and not as his request).
- `archaeology.md`: how the batches came to commit probes, captures and logs, and how the corpus-wide output comparison became standing; by a Sonnet archaeology worker, read-only, from both sessions' transcripts and the commit history. Its findings, in short:
  - No message ever asked Pavol whether a rung's probes, captures, build logs and scratch should go to `main`, and no rule says to commit scratch. The practice is the sum of six small steps, each put in by the coordinator or a worker (section 1).

The coordinator kept the gate's full logs out, which held, and in the same change made ".txt, never .out or .log" the rule for every rung's captures so that `.gitignore` could not catch them, and did not tell him that part stood; its summary to him said "no log files in the repository" (section 8).

This covers the 15 batches' 19 runs in this session, killed and abandoned runs included, but not the probe run or this characterization.

- **Totals**:
  - 269 agents and 27,364 API calls, making 28,826 tool calls over 8,408 agent-min.
  - Output 29.70M estimated, 11.29M recorded.
  - Cache writes 146.03M; cache reads 6,880.8M.
- **The 18 agents that returned nothing** were killed by restarts or interrupts, stopped, failed, or run live again after a missed resume. Together they account for 1.23M output (est.), 10.54M cw, 310.2M cr, 1,268 calls and 472.4 agent-min.
  - The largest single one is 7R's first `rung:J`, cut at 07:36:42 after 184 min: 5.63M cw and 116.1M cr.
  - The next largest are batch 5's first run (2.22M cw, 70.6M cr) and batch 1's first run (0.53M cw, 37.3M cr).

**By stage kind.** The first figure is the share of (estimated output + cache writes); the second is the share of cache reads.

- rung worker (`rung`): 48.7% and 42.3%. It also takes 51.8% of all cache writes, 33.8% of estimated output and 44.2% of agent-minutes.
- first skeptic: 11.4% and 13.9%.
- review: 6.7% and 6.8%.
- gather: 6.1% and 12.7%. It is the second-largest reader.
- rung repair: 5.6% and 6.4%.
- second skeptic: 3.7% and 3.9%.
- rung judge: 3.7% and 1.9%.
- review2: 3.0% and 4.6%.
- judge:review: 2.9% and 1.9%.
- gate: 2.2% and 0.9%.
- repair:review: 2.1% and 2.6%.

- Using recorded instead of estimated output moves the first figure by at most 1.6 points (rung 50.3%, skeptic 10.8%, gather 5.6%), because cache writes are 83% of the sum.

**By family:**

- rung worker (rung, resume): 48.9% and 42.4%.
- review loop (review, judge:review, repair:review, review2): 14.7% and 15.9%.

- 196 requests followed a gap of five minutes or more within the same agent, which is past the cache's five-minute lifetime. They wrote 65.5M, 44.9% of all cache writes. For rung workers it is 70.3% of their 75.6M.

<!-- The process-engineering study Pavol opened on 2026-10-03: what it asks, what is done with where it is, what is pending in order, and what waits on him. Kept current by the coordinator; the boot note points here for the study's state. -->

# The process-engineering study

## The question

Pavol, 2026-10-03, early morning UTC: whether the way the work is run spends the weekly token pool well, and how to divide the pool between improving the process and moving the climb forward. His threads, in his order:

- Why sharing the build between worktrees was called impossible for two weeks, and whether a model given the goal finds the answer ("machine empathy": "this empathy for machine, not wasting resources, is a crucial component of good engineering taste"; "Three seconds versus 0.07 ... if it's better, then let's use it").
- Where each role's tokens go inside a batch, and what is shared between agents that could be done once ("I am perfectly aware that checking and rechecking is the necessary part ... I just want to understand whether that's it").
- Whether one fixed batch workflow, reused for every step of the climb, holds the project back against what a designer would build from the goals alone ("I want to see those designs for the ultra code workflows, but not run them").
- Whether the identical start of every agent can be read from the prompt cache.

## Done

- `cache-sharing.md`: why cache sharing was called impossible (an Opus 5 review's measured "file names differ" written as "cannot be given a warm cache at all", carried by every tier after), the blinded test on both tiers (both found the translation in about 15 minutes given the goal), and the rebuilds priced (245 of 425 builds avoidable over 18 batch runs, about 7.3 hours of agent time, 0.87M tokens: the waste was time, not tokens).
- `p1-cost.md`: how probe P1 wrote 7.0M against a stated 0.5M (19 context rewrites after ten-minute waits its brief did not cap; never put to Pavol). His rule from it: POSITIONS, "The coordinator watches what it launches." (long runs only).
- The blinded engineers' improvements built (`5b0a82d97`; `coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md` section 6): seeded worktrees take the base's file dates (a Java edit's rebuild 143 s to 77 s, and a defect fixed: a branch whose Java differed from the base was never recompiled), and `tools/old-fortress.sh` runs the old code from the base build with a private cache folder (0.04 s, 36 MB, against a 3 s, 206 MB copy per rung). The script and manual change waits for batch 10's landing: the replacement texts are in the coordinator's scratchpad, `old-fortress-script-patch.md`, and the boot note names it.
- `labor.md`: where the tokens of batches 8 and 9 went (14.6M): the fixed start of every agent 19.5%, the agents' own thinking 27%, checking roles 43% against rung workers 37%, exploration beyond the brief about 10% of a worker, 29% of what agents read already given to an earlier agent of the batch; eight levers, together about 1M to 1.5M a batch.
- The first designs for batch 10's goals, `design-batch10-fable.md` (about 5.2M) and `design-batch10-opus.md` (about 4.3M on Opus), from `design-batch10-brief.md`. They are not blind: the record's section 1 carried batch 9's cost by stage, its section 3 lines of the pipeline, POSITIONS and the build-cache note parts of it, and the Opus designer read the record's sections 6 to 8 by a paging slip. Both kept workers, skeptics and a repair round and cut the stages after the rungs.
- The explainer page comparing them with the pipeline and the token measurement: https://claude.ai/artifact/Wy1hJLharoRXVa2uZsr2m6 (source in the coordinator's scratchpad, `design-compare/index.html`).
- The shared-start cache question re-measured (FACTS, "The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box"): only a whole identical prompt is read from the cache; a prompt differing in its last line is written whole again.
- The shared-start question answered by a project agent type (run `wf_e2382567-828`, after the process restart registered `.claude/agents/cache-probe.md`): its system prompt, about 40 KB of text, is written by the first agent and read from the cache by the next two (17,250 read, 3,820 written each); FACTS, "The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box". Untried: a keep-warm agent of the type, and the batch's shared prefix moved into a type.
